name: The rivers turn
note: CLIMATE events. The antagonist with no face, given a body of evidence. Palaeoclimate dating carries real error bars and this file states them as low certainty rather than hiding them; where the reconstruction itself is argued, dispute is set and the trigger is latent. NOT specialist-reviewed.

events.title: The Holocene climatic optimum opens
events.evidence: Speleothem oxygen-isotope records from Mawmluh and Sahiya caves; lake high-stands in the Thar.

events.title: Lunkaransar lake stands full in the Thar
events.evidence: Lake sediment cores and pollen from Lunkaransar and Didwana: freshwater ostracods where there is now sand.

events.title: The summer monsoon reaches its Holocene maximum
events.evidence: Arabian Sea upwelling proxies, speleothem isotopes, and lake levels agreeing across three independent records.

events.title: The sea stands two metres higher than today
events.evidence: Raised beach ridges and mangrove peats along Saurashtra and Kutch. It is why Lothal's basin now sits inland.

events.title: The Rann of Kutch is still a navigable gulf
events.evidence: Marine microfauna in Rann sediments, and Harappan coastal sites now stranded far from water.

events.title: The Ghaggar runs strong and perennial
events.evidence: Palaeo-channel mapping and settlement density along the Ghaggar-Hakra.
events.dispute_text: Whether the Ghaggar was a large perennial Himalayan-fed river at this date, or already a monsoon-fed seasonal one, is actively argued. The identification with the Rigvedic Sarasvati is a further and separate dispute, and a politically live one.

events.title: The Sutlej abandons the Ghaggar for the Indus
events.evidence: Optically stimulated luminescence dating of buried channel sands beneath the Ghaggar plain.
events.dispute_text: Recent OSL work places the Sutlej's avulsion well before the Harappan cities, which would mean the Ghaggar was already seasonal when they were built. Older reconstructions put it much later and make river capture a cause of their decline. The two readings imply opposite stories and the evidence does not yet settle it.

events.title: The Yamuna turns east into the Ganga system
events.evidence: Abandoned channel traces west of the modern Yamuna; sediment provenance studies.
events.dispute_text: Both the timing and whether a single capture event occurred at all are disputed. Some workers see progressive avulsion over millennia rather than one turn.

events.title: Mawmluh Cave becomes the global reference for the 4.2 kiloyear event
events.evidence: The Mawmluh Cave speleothem in Meghalaya, which is the global reference section defining the base of the Meghalayan age.

events.title: The summer monsoon weakens across the northwest
events.evidence: Speleothem and lake records, and the abandonment sequence of the Ghaggar sites.

events.title: Kotla Dahar lake shrinks to a salt pan
events.evidence: Oxygen isotopes in gastropod shells from the Kotla Dahar core in Haryana, showing an abrupt evaporation step.

events.title: The Ghaggar becomes seasonal along its whole course
events.evidence: Channel sedimentology and the eastward drift of settlement away from the Hakra bed.

events.title: The Indus shifts its course past Mohenjo-daro
events.evidence: Flood silts in the upper levels of the city and abandoned channel traces on the plain.

events.title: Winter rainfall retreats from the northwest
events.evidence: Archaeobotany: the winter wheat-barley package gives ground to summer millets and rice.

events.title: The Deccan dries and the Jorwe settlements contract
events.evidence: Settlement contraction at Inamgaon and across the Jorwe sites, with supporting lake evidence.
events.dispute_text: Whether the contraction was driven by drought or by social reorganisation is argued; the two are not mutually exclusive and the evidence supports either reading.

events.title: The Ganga takes Hastinapura
events.evidence: A flood layer in the excavated sequence, and the later textual memory of an abandonment.

events.title: The monsoon strengthens and the eastern clearance accelerates
events.evidence: Speleothem records and the rise of rice agriculture in the middle Ganga.

events.title: The Sudarshana dam bursts in a storm
events.evidence: Rudradaman's Junagadh inscription, which describes the storm, the breach and the repair in unusual technical detail.

events.title: The Sudarshana dam bursts again, and is repaired again
events.evidence: Skandagupta's Junagadh inscription, recording the second breach and reconstruction.

events.title: A warm centuries-long interval steadies the sea route
events.evidence: Northern-hemisphere temperature proxies; the correlation with the Indian Ocean trade boom is suggestive rather than demonstrated.

events.title: A run of failed monsoons in the peninsula
events.evidence: Speleothem growth interruptions in peninsular caves; the Sangam poems' famine imagery is suggestive but not evidence.

events.title: The Kaveri builds its delta seaward
events.evidence: Delta stratigraphy and the inland stranding of former ports such as Kaveripattinam.

events.title: The Godavari delta advances into the bay
events.evidence: Delta-front sediment sequences and the abandonment of older coastal anchorages.

events.title: The medieval climate anomaly: strong monsoons for three centuries
events.evidence: Speleothem records from Dandak and Jhumar caves and from Sahiya, showing sustained high rainfall.
events.note: It coincides exactly with the Chola tank-building programme and the peak of the temple economy. Which caused which is not settled.

events.title: The Kaveri floods across the delta
events.evidence: Inferred from repair endowments in temple inscriptions rather than from a flood record. Generated to stand for a class of event the inscriptions imply and do not date.

events.title: The great tanks begin to silt faster than they are dredged
events.evidence: Tank sediment profiles, and the rising frequency of desilting endowments in the inscriptions.

events.title: The Sri Lankan tank system reaches its greatest extent
events.evidence: The tanks themselves, and the Culavamsa account of Parakramabahu's works.
events.replaces: the tank system at maximum extent

events.title: The Little Ice Age begins and the monsoon weakens
events.evidence: Speleothem and tree-ring records; the correlation with the medieval famine sequence is strong.

events.title: The Durga Devi famine empties the Deccan
events.evidence: Persian and Marathi chronicle accounts of a famine lasting more than a decade. The duration is probably compressed memory of several.

events.title: The Damajipant famine
events.evidence: Chronicle and hagiographical accounts; the date is traditional.

events.title: The Deccan and Gujarat famine
events.evidence: Mughal court records and Dutch and English factory correspondence, which agree on its severity.

events.title: The Doji bara, the skull famine
events.evidence: Company records; and it is one of the earliest famines that can be tied to a documented El Nino event.

events.title: Monsoon failure is understood to follow the Pacific
events.evidence: Walker's statistical work on the Southern Oscillation, undertaken by the India Meteorological Department expressly to forecast famine.

events.title: The Agra famine
events.evidence: Company revenue and relief records.

events.title: The Orissa famine
events.evidence: The Famine Commission report of 1867, which found the deaths avoidable.

events.title: The Great Famine of the south
events.evidence: Famine Commission reports and grain export figures for the same years.

events.title: The Indian famine of 1899
events.evidence: Famine Commission of 1901; the failure of the monsoon that year is instrumentally recorded.

events.title: A cyclone and surge destroy the Hooghly shipping
events.evidence: English and Dutch trading records of shipping losses in the Hooghly, written up months afterwards and at second hand.
events.dispute_text: Contemporary accounts conflate a cyclone with an earthquake reported the same night, and the casualty figures that circulated were later shown to be wildly inflated.

events.title: The Coringa cyclone
events.evidence: Company records of the destruction of the port, which was never rebuilt to its former size.

events.title: The Bengal famine
events.evidence: Provincial and imperial records, the Famine Inquiry Commission of 1945, and price series.
events.dispute_text: That the famine happened and that it killed on the order of millions is not in question. Its causation is: crop shortfall, wartime procurement, the denial policy, provincial trade barriers and refusals of imports have all been argued as primary. The game presents the positions.

events.title: The desert advances across the western dry zone
events.evidence: Dune reactivation dated by luminescence, and the retreat of settlement from the western margin.

events.title: Himalayan glaciers retreat and the rivers run high
events.evidence: Moraine dating in the western Himalaya; the downstream discharge effect is inferred rather than measured.

events.title: The Kashmir valley lakes shrink and the terraces are farmed
events.evidence: Karewa lake sediments and the Neolithic occupation sequence at Burzahom.
